anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
Spec amendments: 2 need your call - from the spec review; applying as recommended reopens no tasks; no phase change.

* crosscut - Share retry policy: move retry policy into one owner. Adapters currently disagree about when to retry.
  Example: adapter-local retry limits -> one coordinator retry limit
  Reviewer: changing retry ownership needs a human architecture choice
  Impact: Design / retries: each adapter sets its own retry policy -> one new retry service sets the retry policy for every adapter
  Recommended: alt-1 (the existing coordinator keeps policy consistent without adding a service).
  Alternatives: alt-1 the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy, and adapters keep execution

* exit126 - Classify blocked execution: classify exit 126 as blocked rather than failed. Operators need to tell a launch problem from a report failure.
  Example: exit 126 = failed -> blocked
  Reviewer: operator-visible status changes need a human decision
  Impact: Design / run status: exit 126 reports a failed run -> exit 126 reports a blocked run
  Recommended: accept (a separate status identifies launch failures).

Reply: 1 (apply all recommendations) | 2: <handle>=<accept|alt-n|custom(<effect>)>, ...
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" to apply every later spec amendment in this flow without asking. That covers corrected facts, paths, and verification lines. It also covers scope, acceptance-criteria, and public-contract edits. A redraw still stops for you: a changed problem statement, or a component that is added, removed, or re-bounded. The grant never replaces a spec approval.

Details
crosscut: Design / retries - old: each report adapter owns its retry policy -> new: a new retry service owns all retry policies
exit126: Design / run status - old: exit 126 is failed -> new: exit 126 is blocked
